data_description.motion_window: How many minutes of motion history to weigh up when deciding where people are.
data_description.suppress_entities: e.g. your doorbell announcement, so background remarks don't talk over it.
data_description.busy_entities: While any of these is on (a meeting calendar, a Focus switch, a phone in Do Not Disturb), Sentient holds back speech that can wait, as if hushed. Safety alerts and replies you ask for still come through. Leave empty to turn this off.
data_description.prompt_memories: How many memories are given to the voice assistant up front. The rest can still be searched.
data_description.pass_through_areas: Hallways, landings and stairs. Walking through these counts for much less, so a passer-by doesn't steal an announcement.
data_description.all_occupied: On: everyone who's home hears it. Off: only the busiest room.
data_description.ai_task_entity: The AI task used for camera looks, briefings, the nightly think and the look at tomorrow. Empty uses Home Assistant's preferred AI task.
data_description.camera_cooldown: A camera watch looks again at most this often, to keep AI costs down.
data_description.fallback_speakers: Only used when nobody is in any other speaker's room, e.g. a living room you'd rather not disturb.
data_description.daily_ai_limit: Background AI calls (camera checks, briefings, the nightly think, the doorbell…) stop for the day after this many, and it uses plain words instead. Questions you ask still get answered. 0 means no limit.
data_description.prompt_recent: A few lines on right now (asleep, hushed or quiet hours, guests, anything open, and readings not heard from for hours so they aren't given as current), what happened in the last hour and where there's been movement, so 'anything I should know?' and 'what just happened?' are answered straight away. Free: no extra AI calls.
data_description.rules: "When this happens, do that" rules (the Rules page), and the voice can make them: it reads the rule back and only saves it after a yes. Rules can never arm, disarm or unlock anything. Off: no rules run.
data_description.relevant_memories: Once there are more memories than fit in the voice's context, it gets the ones that share words with the question, then the newest. Free, no AI. Off: always the newest.
data_description.look_cache_minutes: The same question to the same camera within this time gets the last answer instead of a new AI look. 0 always looks again.
data_description.camera_prefilter: Camera checks and watches compare a tiny picture first (on this machine, free) and only ask the AI when the camera — or its spot — looks different from the last look.
data_description.budget_drive: Its own daily allowance within the overall limit. 0 means it just shares the overall limit.
data_description.budget_noticing: Its own daily allowance within the overall limit. 0 means it just shares the overall limit.
data_description.budget_cameras: Its own daily allowance within the overall limit. 0 means it just shares the overall limit. Safety, the doorbell and questions you ask are never held back.
data_description.routine_evidence: Offers to take over a routine say how often it happened, e.g. '4 of the last 4 weekend days'.
data_description.notice_entities: When these change, the AI decides whether it's worth saying something (or asking). e.g. washing machine, doors, weather, bins.
data_description.remark_repeat_hours: The same thing noticed ("The kettle has finished boiling.") isn't said again for this long. 0: no limit.
data_description.chattiness: Limits remarks per hour: quiet 2, normal 4, chatty 8. Off stops noticing.
data_description.conversation_style: Brief: short, to-the-point answers. Natural: commands stay short, but questions and chat get a few natural sentences and a follow-up question when a person would ask one, which keeps the microphone listening.
data_description.carry_on_minutes: Saying the wake word again this soon after talking carries on the same conversation from the same speaker, so "and upstairs?" still makes sense. 0 turns this off; Home Assistant forgets a conversation after five quiet minutes.
data_description.focused_tools: Give the voice only Sentient's tools that fit what was asked (cameras, heating, reminders…), plus memory and safety. A smaller choice makes cheaper models quicker and more accurate. Anything that doesn't clearly match still gets every tool.
data_description.ask_later: When someone mentions something coming up (a trip, a match, the vet), the voice can remember to ask how it went the next time anyone talks to it — once, never in quiet hours or with guests in, and never about anything private. It never speaks out of the blue. Switching this off forgets anything waiting to be asked.
data_description.put_right: When you say "no, the other one" or "not that light, the lamp", the voice switches back what it just switched (on or off, within a few minutes) and does the request again with only the corrected part — no need to say it all again. Turning this off leaves putting it right to the voice agent.
data_description.music: With Music Assistant set up (or Music through Alexa on): "play something calm in the kitchen" picks from your own playlists and radio stations and plays it on the Music Assistant player in that room (or asks that room's Echo) — at the night volume in quiet hours, and not in a room in its own quiet time unless you're in it. Off: no music tool.
data_description.music_alexa: Without Music Assistant: "play something calm in the kitchen" asks the Echo in that room (Alexa Media Player) to play it from the service below, by name — a playlist, an artist, a song or a mood — at the night volume in quiet hours, and not in a room in its own quiet time unless you're in it. The service must be linked in the Alexa app. Off: the Echos are never asked to play music.
data_description.music_alexa_service: Which service the Echos play from. Spotify works with a free account, but Alexa may shuffle similar music instead of the exact song; Premium plays exactly what's asked for.
data_description.house_rules: Plain sentences every voice must follow, one per line, e.g. 'Never say the house is empty.'
data_description.learn_entities: Lights, switches, fans and blinds people use by hand. Every night the last two weeks are checked for things done at about the same time most days, and for things done straight after something else (a door opening, another light going on).
data_description.learn_anchors: A habit that keeps time with sunset, sunrise or getting up rather than the clock (the lamp at dusk, the blinds at sunrise, the kettle after getting up) is learned that way, so a routine the house does for you moves with the seasons. Getting up needs the asleep and awake setting. Off: everything is learned against the clock, as before.
data_description.offer_together: When a few things usually happen at about the same time on the same days (the lamp on, the blinds closed, the TV on around 8pm), they're offered once, together — one yes and the house does all of them. Off: each is offered on its own.
data_description.trust_lights: When a routine you've let the house take over switches a light: just do it, say so first, or ask and only do it on a yes (nothing happens if nobody answers).
data_description.trust_switches: The same for switches, smart plugs and fans.
data_description.trust_covers: The same for blinds and curtains. Garage doors and gates always ask.
data_description.trust_heating: The same for warming the heating before people are up. Asking first means it can't warm up while everyone's asleep.
data_description.link_triggers: Optional: more things that might set off a habit (the TV starting, a bed sensor…). Doors, windows and the learned lights are always considered.
data_description.suggest_routines: Once per new routine, during the day when someone's home, ask whether the house should do it from now on.
data_description.door_camera: Looked at once when the doorbell rings, to log who came.
data_description.door_triggers: The doorbell button (a binary sensor or event), or anything else that means someone's at the door.
data_description.announce_visitors: Off keeps it to a quiet log that voice assistants can answer from.
data_description.faces: When Frigate (or the doorbell) recognises someone, it goes on the timeline and the voice can answer "has Sam come home?". Names are never announced or guessed — only said when someone asks. Off by default.
data_description.face_people: Names as Frigate knows them. Empty: everyone it recognises.
data_description.face_teach: Helps Frigate's face recognition get better. When someone leaves a chosen camera and Frigate kept a face it couldn't name, the phones get a private "Who's this?" with the face and buttons for the household (phones show three at most). Tapping one teaches Frigate; "Someone else…" takes a typed name for anyone new, or "no" to delete a stranger's face. Never spoken, never on the tablets, at most every ten minutes. Needs Frigate face recognition on and phones chosen for notifications. Off by default.
data_description.face_teach_cameras: Close-up cameras where faces are clear, e.g. the doorbell. Empty: the door camera.
data_description.face_cameras: Empty: every camera. Pick the close-up ones (the doorbell, the front door) so a busy street can't give false names.
data_description.face_forget_hours: Every night, faces Frigate kept but nobody named — strangers, mostly — are deleted from Frigate once they're this old. Named faces are kept. 0: leave it to Frigate (it keeps its last 200).
data_description.clip_watch: When Frigate finishes an event on a chosen camera, the AI watches that stretch of recording once and a sentence goes on the timeline and the Sentient page: "Gate 14:10 — a man walked a dog past". The voice answers "what happened at the gate?" from them without another AI call. Never spoken. Off by default.
data_description.clip_cameras: Start with one, e.g. the gate.
data_description.clip_scope: Frigate's alerts are people in the zones you marked as required — the quietest choice for a busy street. If a camera never makes alerts (no required zones set in Frigate), choose "Anything in a zone" — the Clips card shows what was skipped and why.
data_description.clip_when: Only watch at these times. Away means everyone chosen under Away lights is out.
data_description.clip_notify: Goes to the phones only, with a picture and a play button.
data_description.clip_source: Frigate's own AI review summaries need switching on in Frigate; then no AI call is made here.
data_description.clip_whose: In the same AI call, the household's face photos from Frigate's face library (and the looks below) are included, and it names someone only when it's clearly them — "probably Sam". Strangers are never named. Only said when asked, never announced.
data_description.clip_looks: One per line, e.g. "Sam: red cycling helmet and a yellow coat, on a bike". Helps when a helmet or hood hides the face.
data_description.budget_clips: Counts towards the overall daily AI limit too. 0: no limit of its own.
data_description.clip_days: Summaries are words only, then deleted.
data_description.clip_keep: Off: each clip is deleted as soon as it's been watched.
data_description.parcel_alerts: After a delivery, look again a few minutes later and say if a parcel has been left.
data_description.doorstep_sensors: Optional: person sensors for the doorstep or front garden (e.g. a Frigate zone's person occupancy). When a visit there ends without the bell, the door camera is checked once for a parcel or post left behind.
data_description.zone_visits: Uses the doorstep sensors above (e.g. a Frigate zone's person occupancy). When nobody rings, someone reaching the zone is treated as a visitor: the door camera is looked at and it's announced. Whichever comes first, the bell or the zone, is the visit and the other is ignored. Off: only the bell starts a visit.
data_description.zone_door_sensors: Optional: the front door's open/closed sensor. If the door was opened (or is open) in the last minute and a half, the zone is ignored, because that's someone leaving or coming home.
data_description.face_sensor: Optional: a face-recognition sensor whose state is the name it just recognised (e.g. from Frigate). Used in the log, and in the announcement if that's on.
data_description.sidebar_panel: A page in the sidebar showing memories, routines, watches, visitors and what's been said.
data_description.page_admin_only: Hides the page, and what it reads, from everyone except administrators. Off keeps it open to the whole household. Switching it on does not delete anything.
data_description.custom_pages: On: the Overview, House, Mind and Security tabs use your saved layout, and administrators get EDIT PAGE LAYOUT here to move cards between columns, hide them, show them again or reset a tab. There's no edit button on the tabs themselves, only while you're editing. The layout is saved in Sentient, so every screen shows the same. Off: the tabs go back to the standard layout; your saved layout is kept for when you switch it on again.
data_description.confirm_kinds: Asks the AI to describe these actions and wait for a yes. This is a prompt instruction, not an enforced action block: your conversation agent controls device execution. Turning things off does not need asking. Empty: no extra confirmation instruction. For enforced checks, enable guarded control with its required agent setup.
data_description.auto_backup: Sunday night, a backup of memories, spots, routines, motion lights, shushes and settings, saved in the config folder under sentient_backups.
data_description.suggestions: Things Sentient could use but isn't — a new speaker, a power sensor on the washing machine, a hutch thermometer — offered one line at a time. Yes adds it; no means it's never offered again. Free, no AI.
data_description.whats_new: After Sentient is updated, a short card on the Sentient page says what's new, in plain words, until you tap GOT IT.
data_description.simple_settings: The settings list shows the essentials, with SHOW EVERYTHING for the optional features. New installs start this way. Changes nothing about what Sentient does.
data_description.chat_agent: Who answers the page's Ask box — pick a voice agent that has Sentient ticked. Empty uses your preferred Assist pipeline.
data_description.health_ignore: Entities (and their devices) that shouldn't count as problems, e.g. something that's meant to be off.
data_description.hide_substreams: Leaves out HD and SD streams, screenshots and maps when counting and checking cameras, so one doorbell isn't several cameras. Nothing is deleted from Home Assistant.
data_description.ignore_cameras: Cameras Sentient shouldn't count, check or offer, such as a tablet's camera. They stay in Home Assistant untouched; choose again to bring one back.
data_description.never_entities: Sentient never switches, dims or changes these: not in rules, routines, offers, auto-off, away or motion lights, light shows, the heating or guarded voice control, and the voice is told to leave them alone. It can still read them and talk about them. Anything that would change one is skipped and noted.
data_description.self_check: Each night it looks back over its own records — what it said and how that went down, speakers that failed, things held back, questions asked again and again, the AI meter — and notes what it notices about itself, with the numbers behind it. No AI. Ask "have you been annoying us?" or "what have you realised?".
data_description.learn_corrections: When someone changes back something the house did a moment ago (a light it put on, a routine it took over), it notes the correction. A routine you keep undoing is handed back (switched off) and the timeline says so. Turning this off stops the watching; corrections already noted are kept.
data_description.normal_day: Compares today with what's usual and notes it on the Mind page: for instance nobody up yet when someone usually is by now. Plain rules, nothing is said aloud and nothing is switched. Turning this off stops the checking and hides what it found.
data_description.thoughts: A short first-person list on the Mind page ("people keep switching the landing light back off, so I've stopped"), plus guessing which room someone goes to next and checking how often it was right. No AI. Turning this off stops the guessing and hides the list; what it has learned is kept.
data_description.share_learning: Once an evening (17:00–20:30), when someone's about and it isn't quiet time, it says one thing it has learned or changed its mind about in the last two days: a routine it handed back, a fact it updated, a habit it spotted, how well it now guesses where you go next. Never the same thing twice. Turning this off keeps it all on the Mind page but silent.
data_description.self_adjust: When the self-check finds a kind of remark the house keeps hushing, quieten it a little (the same as a thumbs down; it fades again). Never touches safety, security or anything it controls.
data_description.proposals: When the self-check finds something it got wrong, suggest one small change on the Mind page — fewer remarks, not repeating one so often, a section added to the briefing, a higher AI limit — with the reason. Nothing changes until you say yes; a no isn't asked again for a month. Turning this off clears any waiting suggestions.
data_description.privacy_log: Each AI call and web search Sentient makes is noted — which feature, how many pictures, clips or documents, and which service — never what was said or shown. See it under Brain & system → What leaves the house, with a button to forget the last 48 hours. Turning this off clears the record.
data_description.goals: Let the voice set goals over days or weeks ("help us use less heating this month"). A goal can follow a sensor: it compares each day with the usual week before and mentions progress when it fits. Nothing is changed in the house.
data_description.manuals: Answer questions from the documents in the folder below (one AI call each). Off: the documents are left alone.
data_description.manuals_folder: A folder in Home Assistant’s media (e.g. manuals = media/manuals). Name each file after what it’s for, e.g. "Air purifier.pdf".
data_description.manuals_local_text: When no file name matches the question, look inside .txt and .md documents for the right one, and if the AI can't be reached, read out the closest passage instead of nothing. No AI is used for either. Off: only file names are matched.
data_description.manuals_pages: On: each PDF (and text document) is read once, page by page, into Sentient's own database — on this computer, with no AI. A question then sends the AI only the few pages that match, not the whole document, so it costs far less and the answer says which page it's on ("it's on page 14"). A document whose name doesn't match can still be found by what's in it, and if the AI can't be reached the closest passage is read out with its page. Scanned PDFs (pictures of pages) are still read whole by the AI. Off: documents are read whole every time, and what was read is cleared.
data_description.games: Play voice-led story games, such as an escape-the-flat adventure with the assistants as game master. Each game keeps its own saved memory (where the players are, what they carry, what they found and chose) across sessions and assistants. It is shown to a voice only while a game is being played, and the game master can read the house’s ordinary memory but never change it. Open Settings → Story games to write games and edit their memory. Off: the game tools and page are hidden; saved games are kept, not cleared.
data_description.voice_id: Use the local speaker match for this request. To let the AI model personalise replies or attribute new memories by name, also turn on Share matched names with the conversation agent in Voice Recognition. The separate local “Who’s speaking?” reply is set up in Voice Recognition.
data_description.voice_id_unknown: When an Assist speaker has no voice match, keep the household history and saved memories private for that turn. Off: unmatched voices are treated as normal.
data_description.speaker_memories: With voice recognition running: a matched voice gets their own memories (“Alex: likes tea”) first and never anyone else's personal ones; a voice it can't match gets none of anyone's personal memories. Household facts are always shared. Typed requests and Echos are unchanged. Off by default.
data_description.books: Play audiobooks and read ebooks aloud, keeping each room’s place. "Read my book", "carry on with the book", "read for 20 minutes", "stop", "next chapter", "go back a bit". No AI (except an optional recap). On an Echo: ebooks one passage per request through the Alexa skill; audiobooks need another speaker.
data_description.books_folder: A folder in Home Assistant’s media (books = media/books). DRM-free .epub or .txt ebooks; audiobooks as one .mp3/.m4b/.m4a file, or a folder of parts named after the book.
data_description.reading_tts: A different text-to-speech service just for books and stories — Gemini or ElevenLabs voices are often better storytellers. Leave it blank to read in the usual voice. Echos always use Alexa's own voice.
data_description.reading_voice: Pick the voice from that service. Use TRY THE VOICE below to hear it on the default speaker before saving.
data_description.read_ahead: With a reading voice, the next part of the story is made while this part is read, so a slow voice (a free or cloud one) doesn't leave a gap between parts. Uses that voice a little earlier, never more often.
data_description.recipes: "Let’s make the lasagne": the ingredients, then one step at a time — "next", "repeat that", "go back", "what’s next?" — remembering the step per speaker. "Make it for 6" scales it; ingredients can go on the shopping list.
data_description.recipes_folder: A folder in Home Assistant’s media (recipes = media/recipes) with PDFs, photos, text or Markdown. Each is tidied into steps by one AI call the first time, then kept. Mealie is used automatically if its integration is set up.
data_description.recipes_list: Where "add the ingredients to the shopping list" puts them. Empty: the list with "shopping" in its name.
data_description.tandoor_url: Optional: your Tandoor Recipes address, e.g. http://192.168.1.20:8080.
data_description.tandoor_token: Optional: an API token from Tandoor (Settings → API). Kept in Home Assistant only.
data_description.second_opinion_ai: Optional: a bigger model asked only when the usual one says the picture is too dark or unclear to be sure. Counts towards the daily limit.
data_description.smart_ai_task: Optional. Used only for camera security looks and the overnight think, where a smarter model helps most. Empty: the usual AI, so costs don't change.
data_description.event_clips: Fetches Frigate's short clip of an event and has the AI watch it, so it can say what actually happened ('left a parcel and went'). Used after a camera-security alert, and when asked 'what happened at the door?'. Needs the Frigate integration. One AI call per clip. Off by default.
data_description.notify_targets: Notify entities, e.g. the Home Assistant app on each phone or watch.
data_description.notify_when: Each kind is sent at most once in ten minutes.
data_description.phone_buttons: Through the companion app: at the door — the camera picture and a Show camera button; reminders — Snooze 10 min and Done; questions — when the house wants to ask something (an offer, "want me to do that for you?", or ask-first before doing something) and nobody's near a speaker, it asks on the phones with Yes and No (not in quiet hours). Empty: plain notifications as now.
data_description.phone_apps: e.g. notify.mobile_app_pixel_8. Empty: the companion app behind each phone chosen above (notify.my_phone → mobile_app_my_phone) — never the tablets.
data_description.bins_check: The evening before collection, one camera look at where the bins go out. Only says something if they aren't out: 'Recycling tomorrow, and the bins aren't out yet.' Looks once more an hour later.
data_description.bins_calendar: Empty: a waste-collection calendar from the briefing calendars.
data_description.bins_spot: Drawn on the Spots tab where the bins go out, e.g. 'bins'.
data_description.bins_time: The evening before collection, before quiet hours.
data_description.chime: Off: announcements and questions start straight away, without the speaker's chime.
data_description.welcome_home: When someone gets back after 20 minutes or more, say "Welcome back" in the room they're in — plus what's worth knowing from while they were out (visitors, things that finished, problems). Never in quiet hours, hush or guest mode.
data_description.welcome_people: Empty means everyone with a person entry. You can pick phones (device trackers) instead — handy when a person is set to always be home.
data_description.welcome_min_away: How long someone must have been out before they are welcomed back, in minutes.
data_description.welcome_until: Quiet hours normally hold the welcome back. Set a time and anyone arriving in the evening before it is still welcomed. Leave empty to keep quiet hours as they are.
data_description.speak_volume: Optional: the speaker's volume while Sentient talks, put back afterwards. Empty leaves it alone.
data_description.night_volume: Optional: a quieter level for anything said in quiet hours (urgent messages only).
data_description.duck_media: Anything playing in the same room is turned down while Sentient talks, then turned back up.
data_description.critical_alerts: Smoke, carbon monoxide, gas, water-leak and tamper sensors are found automatically, and so is the alarm going off. Said on every speaker, through quiet hours, hush and guest mode, repeated twice while still on, and sent to phones.
data_description.energy_insight: Today's use of the devices on the Energy dashboard compared with the past week: the Energy card, the briefing section, the voice tool and notes on unusual use. Off hides and stops all of it.
data_description.energy_price: Optional: your unit rate per kWh, to show today's cost of the Energy dashboard's devices — in pence or cents (24.5) or in pounds, dollars or euros (0.245); either works.
data_description.energy_currency: The currency costs are shown in. Empty: Home Assistant's own currency (Settings → System → General).
data_description.price_entity: Your electricity price now, from your supplier's integration (Octopus Energy, Nordpool…). If it lists the coming rates they're used; otherwise the usual price at each hour is learned from the last week. Once per appliance (washing machine, dishwasher, dryer) it asks in the evening whether you'd like a nudge to use the delay start when it's cheapest overnight. Empty: off.
data_description.search_hints: When Voice Satellite LLM Tools (or Sentient's own search) is set up, the voice is told the search tools are there and to use them for anything outside the house — words on a speaker, pictures only on a tablet. No AI calls of its own.
data_description.web_search: A voice-only web search through your own SearXNG (for example the SearXNG add-on). Only used when Voice Satellite LLM Tools' web search isn't installed, so the voice never gets two. Off by default.
data_description.searxng_url: For example http://localhost:8080 or the add-on's address. SearXNG must allow the json format (in its settings: search → formats).
data_description.alexa_skill: Adds nothing until a skill uses it: point an Alexa skill (for example the community 'Home Assistant Assist' skill) at the 'For Alexa' agent, then say “Alexa, ask” and your skill's name. Off by default.
data_description.alexa_wait: Alexa hangs up after about 8 seconds, so the answer must come quicker than this.
data_description.alexa_late_answers: When the AI takes longer, Alexa says “Give me a moment” and the answer is said on the same Echo when it's ready.
data_description.left_open_minutes: Said once (then every half hour while still open), within quiet hours and shushes as usual. 0 turns it off.
data_description.leaving_check: When the last person leaves, anything open or unlocked goes on the timeline and to phones ("Left open").
data_description.critical_extra: Anything else that should always be said everywhere when it turns on, e.g. a panic button or a freezer-too-warm sensor. An alarm panel going off is always included.
data_description.heating_entities: Thermostats to learn from. Leave empty for every one in the house. It learns how fast each warms up and the temperature it's usually set to.
data_description.preheat: Start the heating early so it's at the usual temperature by the time people normally get up. A thermostat with its own schedule is put back on it afterwards, and one that's switched off is left off.
data_description.heating_schedule: On: the heating times made on the House tab run (a thermostat set to a temperature, or off, at a time on chosen days), and only on the thermostats chosen there. Off: none run and the schedule is hidden; the times you've saved are kept and run again when this is switched back on.
data_description.comfort_temp: Optional: the temperature to warm up to. Leave empty to use the one it's usually set to during the day.
data_description.inside_sensors: Optional: which motion sensors mean someone's inside. Leave empty to use the ones on the same floors as the speakers (garden and camera sensors don't count). Used for night watch and getting-up times.
data_description.weekly_report: On Sunday evenings, put what the house learned and noticed this week on the timeline (sent to phones if digests are).
data_description.night_watch: Learns when each door, gate and window normally opens. An opening at a time it never usually does, with nobody moving inside first, is an alert. If someone was up inside (leaving for work, say), it's only noted.
data_description.night_watch_entities: Leave empty for every door, window, gate and garage door sensor.
data_description.night_watch_announce: An unusual opening with nobody up is said straight away, through quiet hours, hush and guest mode — it could be someone who shouldn't be there.
data_description.warm_by_weekdays: Optional: when it should be warm on weekdays. Leave empty to use the learned getting-up time.
data_description.warm_by_weekends: Optional: the same for Saturdays and Sundays.
data_description.heating_limit: When someone turns up or switches on one of the heating thermostats chosen above, by voice or in the app, put it back (to its schedule; a thermostat with no schedule goes back to how it was, even off) after this many hours. Only those thermostats; 0 (the default) never does.
data_description.heating_night_temp: Where the heating schedule drops to when a period ends, and the night level it keeps. The schedule never switches a thermostat off. Change it here whenever you like (5–28°C).
data_description.heating_revert_day_hours: How long a change made while a heating period is running is left alone before the schedule takes over again.
data_description.heating_revert_night_hours: How long a change made outside the heating periods (including switching the heating off) is left alone. At night the heating goes back to the night temperature, never off.
data_description.personality: How the house sounds — in remarks, briefings, welcomes and to every voice assistant.
data_description.personality_notes: Optional, in your own words, e.g. 'Fond of the cats. Teases gently about how much tea gets made.'
data_description.style_feedback: A button next to the thumbs on anything it said: pick Shorter, Plainer, Less cheeky, More detail, or say how. The notes below are then followed everywhere it speaks. Off: no button, and the notes aren't used.
data_description.style_notes: One per line; added from the button, and yours to edit. The latest 8 are used.
data_description.camera_security: Follow people from camera to camera, and alert for someone in the garden when the gate and doors didn't open, or anyone about at night with nobody up. Alerts are said out loud in quiet hours if night watch does.
data_description.camera_security_sensors: Each camera's (or zone's) person sensor, e.g. Frigate's 'Gate person occupancy'.
data_description.camera_security_inside: The person sensors for places behind the gate or fence — the garden, the shed. Someone appearing there without a way in opening is an alert.
data_description.camera_security_entries: The gate and doors people should come through (e.g. the back gate and the back door).
data_description.camera_security_describe: One AI look at the camera for each alert ('a man in a dark hoodie trying the shed door').
data_description.security_reasoning: Before a camera-security alert is said out loud, look at the alarm, whether everyone is out, an entry door or gate that opened just before, indoor movement, Frigate events and how often that camera has already alerted. Someone probably going out, or the same camera again within half an hour, is kept quiet. The alert still goes on the timeline and to phones, with the reasons. The alarm set or everyone out: always said. No AI. Off by default.
data_description.party_lights: The lights that join in when not using the whole house. Leave empty to use the room of whoever asks (or say a room: 'disco mode in the living room').
data_description.party_style: Disco: quick colour changes. Party: bright colours, short fades. Rainbow: a colour wheel. Chill: slow, dim colours. Halloween: flickering orange, purple and green. Christmas: red, green and warm white, twinkling.
data_description.party_minutes: Then every light goes back exactly as it was. 0 keeps going until it's turned off.
data_description.party_whole_house: Every light that can dim or change colour joins in (light groups, screens and backlights don't). Say 'disco mode everywhere' to do this just once.
data_description.party_exclude: Left out of every show, even 'everywhere' — tablet screens, a projector, a bedroom where someone sleeps.
data_description.party_sound: Optional: a loudness sensor in dB, such as a voice speaker's microphone through ESPHome's sound_level sensor. Disco, party, rainbow and Halloween then follow the music — louder is brighter, and each beat changes colour.
data_description.party_show: Which shows get a button on the overview. Leave empty for none; every show still works by voice.
data_description.party_sound_switch: Optional: a switch that makes the loudness sensor report (so it isn't sending readings all day). It's turned on while a show follows the sound and off afterwards. Found automatically if it's on the same device and has 'loudness' in its name.
data_description.room_volume: Speakers that can hear the room (a loudness sensor on the same device) have a one-second listen first and speak louder over a TV or chatter. Not in quiet hours.
data_description.follow_you: Something said where nobody was about — or held back for quiet hours — is passed on the next time someone walks into a room with a speaker.
data_description.follow_minutes: After this long an unheard message is dropped.
data_description.conversation_memory: Keeps a short record of what was asked and said on every speaker, so another room can pick up where one left off. Kept two weeks; private while guests are in.
data_description.follow_ups: Voices can set follow-ups ("I'll check the room's warmed up in an hour") and a watch that runs out with nothing seen is closed off out loud.
data_description.curiosity: At most once a day, when someone's about, it asks about something it can't explain — a regular caller, a pattern it noticed overnight — and remembers the answer.
data_description.reflection: One AI call each night over the day's log and conversations: new things worth remembering, a thought or two for the morning, and a question to ask.
data_description.drive_spot: The camera spot that shows the drive (draw it on the Spots tab).
data_description.drive_camera: Only needed if more than one camera has a spot with that name.
data_description.drive_triggers: Motion or car sensors that see the drive. Empty: the camera's own motion and car sensors.
data_description.camera_wake: Actions that wake a camera from standby (a wake or refresh button, a stream switch, a script). {{ camera }} is the camera about to be looked at. Empty: cameras are looked at as they are.
data_description.camera_wake_cameras: Empty: every camera the AI looks at.
data_description.camera_wake_seconds: Seconds to wait after waking, for a fresh picture.
data_description.known_cars: One per line, e.g. 'Sam: dark grey hatchback'. The same look at the drive then says whose car arrived ('Sam's car arrived on the drive') — no extra AI. Empty: cars aren't named.
data_description.full_volume_speakers: Announcements on these are said at 100%, then the volume goes back — for tablets turned down for everything else. Not in quiet hours (the quiet-hours volume is used then).
data_description.tts_entity: Speakers can be Assist speakers or media players. Echos are spoken to through Alexa Media Player; any other media player (a smart speaker, a Cast device) uses this text-to-speech voice.
data_description.speak_house_language: Translate ordinary English sentences using the existing AI task, with a time limit, temporary sentence cache and original-text fallback. Urgent alerts never wait for AI. Use Automatic language support for prepared phrases and conversation endings; select the language below. Fixed exact yes/no tokens cover common languages. Personal sentence translations are never saved across restarts.
data_description.speakers: Assist speakers or media players (Echos through Alexa Media Player).
data_description.media_speakers: Off: only the voice speakers are used, even where an alarm or announcement names an Echo (it goes where people are instead). Also an 'Echo speakers' switch for automations and dashboards.
data_description.media_important_only: On: the Echos only say alarms, reminders and safety alerts; announcements, notices and chat go to the voice speakers instead. Also an 'Echos: alarms and reminders only' switch.
data_description.foresight: Each evening one AI look at tomorrow's calendars, weather, alarms and reminders. Says something only when there's something to do tonight — frost before an early start, rain on washing day. Usually silent.
data_description.sleep_detection: Asleep after a bedtime routine, or in quiet hours once nothing inside has moved for a while. Awake in the morning when there's movement in two rooms (or a light switched on by hand). A House sensor shows it.
data_description.bedtime_routines: Routines that mean everyone's gone to bed, comma separated. Empty: any routine with 'night' or 'bed' in its name.
data_description.sleep_actions: e.g. tablet screens off, the Echo speakers switch off.
data_description.wake_actions: e.g. the Echo speakers back on, the hallway light on low.
data_description.appliances: Washing machine, dryer, dishwasher, hoover — their power sensor or status. Leave empty to follow every robot vacuum and any power sensor named washing machine, dryer or dishwasher.
data_description.appliance_announce: Says “the washing machine's finished” where people are, and when one is taking far longer than usual. Plain words, no AI.
data_description.appliance_watts: For power sensors: running while above this, finished once it's stayed below for five minutes.
data_description.voice_agent: The AI agent that normally answers (e.g. Google AI). Empty uses the page's chat agent.
data_description.backup_agent: Answers when the main agent fails — Home Assistant's own agent does lights, heating and timers without any AI.
data_description.offline_answers: When the AI agent fails, “is the house locked up?”, “when's my next alarm?” and “did anyone come round?” are answered straight from the house, in plain words, before the backup agent is tried. Only questions, only what the person may see; in guest mode only the security question. Off: everything goes to the backup agent.
data_description.animal_sensors: Hutch, kennel, coop or tank temperature sensors.
data_description.away_lights_on: When everyone's out after dark, the lights copy how they were used at the same time last week (from Home Assistant's history), a few minutes either way. Doesn't start (or stops) if anyone's home or there's been movement inside lately, for people without a phone tracked, and puts back what it switched on. Also an 'Away lights' switch.
data_description.away_people: Empty: everyone with a person entry. You can pick phones (device trackers) instead of people.
data_description.away_lights: Empty: every light in a room, leaving out screens, LED rings, backlights and groups. Only lights that were used at that time last week come on.
data_description.holiday_mode: A 'Holiday mode' switch, and 'we're going on holiday until Sunday' by voice. While it's on, nothing is said out loud except safety alerts — what would have been said goes to the phones chosen for notifications, with visitors and parcels; the away lights run even if they're normally off; and the thermostats below are turned down. Off: no switch and no holiday by voice.
data_description.holiday_thermostats: Turned down to frost protection while you're away, and put back exactly as they were when holiday mode ends. Empty: the heating isn't touched.
data_description.holiday_frost: What the thermostats above are set to while you're away.
data_description.holiday_end_on_return: Once everyone has gone out, the first person home ends holiday mode and puts the heating back. Off: it ends on its date or when switched off.
data_description.away_after: So popping to the shop doesn't start it.
data_description.animal_low: Says once when it drops below this (held until morning in quiet hours), and warns the evening before a frost.
data_description.animal_high: Says once when it rises above this.
data_description.hutch_check: Half an hour after sunset, one AI look at the hutch: are they in, and is it shut? Only says something if not.
data_description.hutch_spot: The spot drawn round the hutch on the Spots tab, e.g. 'rabbit pen'.
data_description.cat_watch: After dark, when a cat sensor on the hutch's camera goes on, one AI look: is a cat at or by the hutch? At most every 15 minutes, and not when the picture hasn't changed.
data_description.cat_sensors: Empty: the cat sensors on the hutch's camera (e.g. Frigate's cat occupancy).
data_description.cat_loud: Off: kept for the morning ('A cat was by the hutch at 2:14am'). On: said at once through the night-watch speakers.
data_description.rain_warnings: When rain's due within the hour and a window or door is open: 'Rain's on the way in the next hour, and the bedroom window's open.' Reads the hourly forecast — no AI. Once per spell of rain.
data_description.rain_entities: Empty: every window and door sensor.
data_description.self_test: Overnight, the voice is asked a few everyday questions (the temperature outside, anything open, reminders, the alarm, the time) and its answers are checked against the house. Anything wrong shows in house health with the tool it used. About 5 AI calls a run. Questions only — nothing is switched.
data_description.screen: Alerts, notices and a morning card on the Sentient screen card (custom:sentient-screen-card). Off: it only shows the house at a glance.
data_description.screen_actions: e.g. wake a tablet and switch it to the page with the screen card.
data_description.screen_clear_actions: e.g. switch the tablet back to its normal page.
data_description.conversation_sessions: Use the Sentient with backup agent. Single commands stop listening unless the spoken reply ends in a question. Information, security, health and system discussions ask if there is anything else and stay open until you say “that’s all”, “enough” or “stop listening”, or the inactivity timeout expires. Say “back to the…” to resume an unfinished topic from this device within 24 hours, without restoring action permissions. The Mind panel shows recent conversation decisions. Follow-up listening needs a compatible Assist device.
data_description.room_conversation_handoff: Say carry on with and name a topic from another device. Both requests must come from the same identified Home Assistant user. Fresh readings are checked and earlier actions and confirmations do not carry over.
data_description.verified_bedtime: Say run downstairs bedtime to switch off the selected lights and check the selected contacts. Ask downstairs bedtime status to recheck, or say cancel downstairs bedtime to stop tracking it.
data_description.verified_bedtime_lights: Choose up to twenty individual Assist-exposed lights. Groups are excluded and the Never touch list still applies.
data_description.verified_bedtime_contacts: Choose up to twenty Assist-exposed door, window or other opening contacts to check. They are read only.
data_description.session_seconds: Discard session context and pending actions after this many seconds without another turn. Your voice device controls its own silence timeout. Confirmation also expires after 60 seconds.
data_description.guarded_control: Opt in with a dedicated supported AI agent: select only Sentient guarded under Control Home Assistant, then use Sentient with backup in the pipeline. Turn off Prefer handling commands locally and remove conflicting sentence triggers, which run before this agent. Wrong agent API configuration stops requests. No unrestricted fallback, scripts, scenes or alarm actions. Doors, appliance starts and significant heating changes require a separate yes.
data_description.routine_verify: On: after a voice routine (goodnight, leaving…) runs, each light, switch, lock and cover it changed is checked a few seconds later, and the answer says what didn't happen ("Done, except the landing light, which is still on"). Steps it can't check (scripts, scenes) are reported as not checked, never as done. Nothing is retried or undone by itself. Off: routines run as before, unchecked.
data_description.voice_unlock: Lets enforced voice confirmation unlock a door after a separate yes. Off (the default) keeps locking and closing but refuses to unlock or open by voice, because Sentient cannot tell who is speaking.
data_description.voice_undo: With guarded control, say “undo that” to request restoration of recent verified light settings. Skips lights changed since, expires with the session, and never undoes locks, heating or appliances.
data_description.evidence_awareness: Tell the voice to distinguish observations, inferences, attempted actions and verified device reports. Unavailable security sensors always prevent an all-secure claim.
data_description.security_incidents: Group configured camera-security person sensors and entry contacts with alerts and clip summaries. Keep seven days locally. Time proximity is a possible link, not proof of the same person; only escalating alerts repeat.
data_description.incident_front: Cameras and sensors at the front of the house (the doorbell, the front door). Anything here is never grouped into one security incident with anything that isn't, and the other way round: someone at the front door and someone at the back gate at the same moment are two incidents. Leave empty to group by time alone.
data_description.live_voice_check: Show the user-started voice check in the Mind panel. Turning this off clears the current check and stops recording check turns. Requires Conversation sessions to start a check.
data_description.speech_delivery_history: Keep recent per-speaker announcement results in the Mind panel. Turning this off clears this history. Speaker failure detection and safe retry handling remain active.
data_description.alexa_tts_only: Use plain TTS instead of Alexa announcements if announcements are unreliable. This bypasses Alexa announcement chimes; other speakers are unchanged.
data_description.update_checker: Check GitHub for stable releases when enabled, at startup and every six hours. No AI calls, automatic installation or automatic restarts. Disable to stop checks.
data_description.contextual_followups: Requires Conversation sessions and the Sentient with backup agent. Keep the subject for short follow-ups, refresh exposed device readings, and clarify ambiguous adjustments. Does not grant action permissions or change listening rules. Off by default; turning it off clears temporary conversation context.
data_description.conversation_recovery: Requires Conversation sessions and the Sentient with backup agent. Cancel a pending or running request from the same conversation/device/user, and avoid replaying uncertain device commands after an AI failure. Cannot undo an action already sent or make hardware accept speech while busy. Off by default; disabling stops this extra handling.
data_description.automatic_language: Requires Say built-in sentences in the house language. Prepare common phrases, conversation endings and safety labels with your existing AI and budget. Off by default. Phrases stay in memory unless Remember common language phrases is enabled. Disabling clears them. Urgent alerts never wait for AI; generated replies never authorise critical actions.
data_description.voice_language: Use auto for Home Assistant’s language, or a language code such as es, de or pt-BR. Requires the speech language option. Your Assist speech recognition and TTS voice must also support this language; this does not reconfigure them.
data_description.remember_language_phrases: Requires both speech language options. Save only the generic phrase pack across restarts and unrelated Settings changes, never personal announcements. Off by default. Disabling, changing language/provider, or forgetting data clears it.
data_description.stream_voice_replies: Starts speaking a long reply while the AI is still writing it, even with conversation sessions on, so answers begin sooner. If Sentient changes the reply afterwards (a confirmation question, for example), the change is spoken after what was already said. Off by default; switching it off returns to waiting for the whole reply. Nothing is stored.
data_description.voice_timing_diagnostics: Keep the last 20 voice response timings in memory, without transcripts or device/user IDs. Show agent, tool, translation and announcement timings in Mind. Stages can overlap; microphone capture and final pipeline playback are not measured. Off by default; Settings changes and forgetting clear the history.
data_description.specific_clarification: Requires Conversation sessions. Offer named device choices and recognise exact names, English ordinals, both/all, and simple temperatures locally. One retry, then stop rather than repeat. Selection never confirms an action. Off by default; disabling clears pending choices. Use guarded control for enforced action restrictions.
data_description.action_recovery: Requires Conversation sessions and guarded control for device results and retries. Give named partial results and inspect the last guarded request when you say that did not work. Only actions never dispatched can be offered again, with fresh confirmation. Uncertain or successful actions are not replayed. Off by default; records expire after two minutes and clear on Settings changes or forgetting.
data_description.recheck_unconfirmed: When a device controlled through guarded voice control hasn't reported its new state by the time of the reply (a garage door, a slow cloud plug), look once more 20 seconds later and update the record, so “did that work?” is answered from what the device says now. Nothing is sent again. Off: the record stays as it was at the reply.
data_description.speech_failure_notification: Show a Home Assistant notification when speaker delivery fails or is uncertain. Off by default. Does not include spoken content or repeat speech. Disabled in guest mode; existing notifications remain until dismissed.
data_description.recent_followup_context: Use a recently completed subject after a fresh wake word on the same speaker and user. Requires conversation sessions and contextual follow-ups. Uses the session timeout; never restores confirmation or listening. Off by default. Ending or forgetting clears context.
data_description.conversation_cues: Within a conversation: everyday sign-offs (“cheers”, “perfect, thanks”, “that'll do”) end it when nothing specific is waiting for an answer; “sorry, I meant…”, “wrong light” and “not the lamp, the ceiling light” are corrections; and “on another note…” or “something else:” starts a fresh subject with no devices carried over. No AI. Off: only the plain endings and corrections are recognised.
data_description.behaviour_explanations: Answer short questions about listening and recorded device results directly, without an AI call. Requires conversation sessions. Uses existing session records, respects guest mode and device access, and never repeats an action. Off by default; no additional history is stored.
data_description.current_house_context: Give conversations a compact relevant snapshot of exposed device reports, recent changes and the current unfinished task. Off by default. No background AI calls. Guest mode suppresses it. Recent changes expire after 30 minutes; disabling or forgetting clears memory-only context.
data_description.house_context_entities: Devices to include in general house summaries, alongside automatic climate and opening/presence reports. Only currently exposed and accessible devices are shared; at most eight relevant readings per request.
data_description.house_context_updates: Requires current house context. After a verified guarded heating request, optionally say once when that thermostat reports the requested temperature. Expires after one hour, cancels if its target changes, at most one update per 15 minutes. Respects normal speech rules and guest mode. Off by default. Turning off clears pending updates.
data_description.security_event_evidence: Use Frigate event IDs, snapshots and clips on configured cameras. A unique camera/time match is a candidate link, not proof that a sensor identified that event. Keep up to 3,000 event records for seven days, locally. Off by default. Disabling hides links and stops matching; retained records expire or can be forgotten.
data_description.security_event_zones: Only what enters a zone: on a camera with Frigate zones, an event is listed (and can start a security incident) only once the object has entered one of them, the same rule Frigate uses for its alerts. A camera without zones lists everything. Anything detected: every object Frigate tracks on the chosen cameras. Frigate's own settings are never changed.
data_description.security_event_hidden_zones: One per line as camera/zone, for example gate/driveway. Events that are only ever in these zones aren't listed and don't start security incidents. Use HIDE THIS ZONE on the Security page after a few 'not a person' corrections there, or remove a line to list that zone again. Frigate isn't changed.
data_description.security_coverage: Show which configured cameras contributed retained evidence and any unavailable reports recorded alongside live incidents. Current camera reports are shown separately. Turning this off clears retained coverage gaps.
data_description.frigate_pipeline_health: Read Frigate MQTT availability, per-camera processing rates and when Sentient last received an event. Missing data is shown as unknown. No camera settings are changed.
data_description.security_conversation_context: Remember the selected event for up to five minutes within the same conversation, device and user. Follow-up questions use that event and fresh occupancy reports; no identity or continued presence is assumed. Tracks configured camera events. Off by default. Disabling clears conversation references; event records retain their normal expiry.
data_description.security_event_feedback: Admins can mark a visit a good catch, not a person, or one to ignore. Reviewed visits move into a folded Reviewed list, and 'not a person' also counts as a reviewed false detection for a security incident made only of that visit. Corrections stay for seven days. No automatic detector, alarm or notification-rule changes. Disabling hides feedback and stops new corrections; use Forget recent data to erase retained records.
data_description.share_clip_analysis: Share compatible generic analyses of the same finished Frigate event across automatic clip watching and event-clip questions. Provider, footage coverage and identity settings must match. Custom questions are analysed separately. Keep at most 100 results in memory for six hours. Off by default. Disabling, changing settings or forgetting clears the cache.
data_description.sleep_ignore_sensors: Motion sensors that fire while people are asleep, such as one in a bedroom. Going to sleep waits for nothing to move for the time above; a bedroom sensor that triggers as someone turns over would keep the house "awake" all night, so list it here. They still count for everything else.
data_description.heating_graph: On: the heating card on the House tab shows the last 24 hours of each thermostat's temperature against what it was set to, with the scheduled times shaded. Read from Home Assistant's history; nothing extra is stored. Off: the graph is hidden.
data_description.heating_revert: On: if a thermostat is turned up, down or off by hand (or changes itself) and isn't back on the schedule, Sentient leaves it for a while and then puts it back: the period's temperature in the day, the night temperature at night. Only thermostats in a heating schedule. Off: changes by hand stay until the next scheduled time. Nothing is stored either way.
data_description.rooms_view: On: the House tab shows a tile for each room — temperature, humidity, lights on, doors and windows open, when someone last moved there and what's playing — and the overview gets a short around-the-house card. Built from your areas; nothing is stored. Off: both are hidden.
data_description.outdoor_areas: Areas that are outside the house, such as a rabbit hutch, shed or greenhouse. They still get their own tile on the House tab, marked OUTSIDE, and their temperature is shown on its own line on the overview, but they are left out of the warmest and coolest room. Leave empty to count every area as part of the house.
data_description.knowledge_card: On: the Mind tab sums up what it has learned about the house — usual bedtime and getting-up time, sensors it is setting aside, how quickly the heating warms, next-room guesses, routines and memories. It only shows what is already known; nothing extra is stored. Off: the card is hidden.
data_description.day_chart: On: the overview shows today hour by hour — movement, what it said, what happened outside and what you asked it — with when someone was first up and the busiest hour. Counted from the timeline; nothing extra is stored. Off: the chart is hidden.
data_description.house_ledger: On: every change to every device is recorded with what caused it (a person, a voice request, an automation, Sentient, or nothing in Home Assistant, meaning the device itself, its app or someone at it), so you can ask "when did the heating go off, and why?". Fast-changing numbers are kept as notable changes. Kept 90 days in Sentient's own database, then summarised by day. Off: nothing new is recorded; what was kept stays until you clear it on the Mind tab.
data_description.unexplained_changes: On: when a watched device (by default the heating, water heaters and valves) changes with nothing in Home Assistant behind it at a time that's unusual for it, it is said once and put on the timeline, and repeats are linked: "the third time this week, always around 11am". While it is still learning a device, or once a repeat becomes usual, it only goes on the timeline. Off: still recorded, never mentioned.
data_description.unexplained_entities: Leave empty for the heating, water heaters and valves. Locks, doors and gates are used by hand every day, so add them only if you want to hear about them.
data_description.expectations: On: learns how often each device changes at each hour, on weekdays and at weekends (warmed up from the last three weeks of history), and scores every change from usual to very unusual. The Mind tab shows how much of each day it expected. Plain counting, no AI. Off: no scores; clear what it learned on the Mind tab.
data_description.surprise_gating: Watch: notes which remarks it would skip because the change is usual for the time, without skipping any. On: skips them, which also saves the AI call. Never applies to safety alerts, alarms or anything you asked for.
data_description.situations: On: the voice is told a few plain lines of what's going on now (just got home, movement in the last 15 minutes, anything unusual in the last hour). Not shared with guests or in a private room. Off: nothing extra is sent.
data_description.beliefs: On: each night it looks for things that keep happening by themselves at about the same time, tests each one against the day just gone, asks about one that holds, and drops ones that don't. No AI. Off: no new beliefs and no testing; existing ones are cleared with the learning on the Mind tab.
data_description.learn_reactions: On: something Sentient switched that's put straight back counts against doing it again, and a remark someone acts on counts in its favour. Off: reactions aren't scored.
data_description.ai_case_memory: On: a background AI job identical to one in the last six hours reuses that answer instead of another call. Never used for pictures or clips. Off: every job calls the AI, and the saved answers are cleared.
data_description.voice_speed_watchdog: On: notices when a speaker takes far longer to hear you than you took to speak (its audio arriving slower than real time) and puts it in the timeline with a restart suggestion. Off: no check.
data_description.voice_speed_restart: On: a speaker that keeps lagging is restarted with its own restart button. Off: it's only suggested.
data_description.incident_stages: On: each security incident shows how far it has got — observed, investigating, likely household, concerning or resolved — from what was recorded, never who someone was. Off: incidents are listed without a stage.
data_description.cognitive_shadow: On: a second, stricter way of judging each security incident runs alongside the usual stages and counts how often the two agree, with how actions by voice turned out, shown on the Mind sensor as totals only (no names, pictures or devices). It is for testing: it never changes an alert, a stage, what is said or what the voice is told. Off: nothing is compared, and the counts start again.
data_description.cognitive_decides: On: once your reviews of security incidents (the buttons under each incident on the Mind tab) show it gets each kind right — at least 10 reviewed household incidents with 90% agreeing, at least 10 others it hardly ever calls household, and no concerning incident called less serious — the cognitive core decides the stage of each incident: what the Mind tab and the voice say an incident is. It stops by itself if later reviews fall short, and says so on the timeline. It never changes or holds back an alert, and never calls an incident less serious than the usual rules' "concerning". Until it has earned it, nothing changes. Off: the usual rules decide; your reviews are kept.
data_description.cognitive_quiet_heads_up: Testing only: records eligibility based on incident reviews, but never suppresses spoken or phone security alerts. Gate opening followed by a camera person detection does not establish household identity. The feature cannot silence anything until independently verified identity evidence has been implemented and tested.
data_description.weather_warnings: On: official warnings for your country are checked every 30 minutes (Met Office and Environment Agency in the UK, MeteoAlarm across Europe, the National Weather Service in the US), using Home Assistant's location. Off: no checks, and what was found is forgotten.
data_description.warnings_country: Leave empty to use Home Assistant's country.
data_description.warnings_region: Only warnings naming this region, e.g. North West England. Leave empty for all of the country (flood and US warnings are always near home).
data_description.warnings_speak: On: a new amber, red or severe warning is said once. Off: warnings only go on the timeline.
data_description.email_read: On: keeps the sender, subject and a short preview of the last 20 messages Home Assistant's IMAP integration reports, so you can ask "any new email?". Read-only, no password, never shared with guests. Off: nothing is kept and what was kept is cleared.
data_description.calendar_clashes: On: "any clashes tomorrow?" finds events that overlap, or with under 15 minutes between, in the briefing's calendars (or all calendars). Off: not offered.
data_description.security_audit: On: an admin can ask "is my setup secure?" for a read-only check of plain-http remote access, locks and alarms the voice can reach without a confirmation, long-lived tokens and admins without two-factor login. Off: not offered.
data_description.automation_builder: On: an admin can ask for an automation in plain English; every device and action is checked, it's read back for a yes, then saved to automations.yaml like one from the editor. Off: not offered; automations already made stay.
data_description.pronounce_names: On: a name the voice reads wrongly from its spelling is said the way it's pronounced, on speakers only — the chat, timeline and phones keep the real spelling. Taken from the lines below and from memories such as "Siobhan is pronounced Shivawn". Off: names are read as spelt.
data_description.pronunciations: Written = said, one per line, e.g. Siobhan = Shivawn. Spell the said version the way the voice should read it.
data_description.health_duplicates: On: a device that appears twice under one name where one copy is empty (a plug in Tuya Local and again from Tuya's cloud) is shown in House health, with a button to disable the empty copy. Off: not checked.
data_description.manuals_local_ocr: Optional and off by default. If Tesseract is already installed on the Home Assistant host, read text from up to 20 image-only PDF pages per file. No cloud requests or downloads. On standard Home Assistant OS, Tesseract may be unavailable; the original PDF fallback remains.
data_description.memory_semantic_enabled: Off by default. With an explicitly configured local Ollama embedding service, rerank only memory results already permitted to this user. Private text is sent to the configured LAN host, never automatically to the internet. The configured host receives selected memory snippets, so run it on a trusted machine you control.
data_description.memory_semantic_url: An HTTP URL such as http://192.168.1.20:11434. Only numeric private LAN/loopback addresses are accepted (use 127.0.0.1 instead of localhost). The server must expose /api/embed and already have the model installed.
data_description.memory_semantic_model: The name of an embedding model already installed in Ollama, such as nomic-embed-text. Sentient will not download the model. Unavailable or slow services fall back to normal search.
data_description.ai_routing_enabled: Off by default. Only eligible background text jobs may use the configured alternative after both providers have 20+ measured calls and sufficient service-level reliability. No switching for pictures, structured output or explicit AI selections.
data_description.ai_routing_alternative: A second Home Assistant ai_task entity to consider for suitable background text tasks. It must exist locally and is never used without measured service history and cost estimates.
data_description.ai_routing_primary_cost: Your own approximate price for one comparable text job; not provider billing. Both prices must be supplied and verified by you before a cheaper provider is considered.
data_description.ai_routing_alternative_cost: Your own price estimate for the alternative AI Task entity. This is not live billing and may differ from real token charges.
data_description.ai_routing_max_p95_ms: Only consider the secondary provider when its measured 95th-percentile service time is within this limit. Defaults to 4000 ms. Voice replies continue through their existing pipeline.
data_description.heating_energy_sensor: A cumulative kWh energy sensor measuring the heating system, not the whole house. Use a sensor retained by Recorder with long-enough history.
data_description.heating_measurement_date: The date of the change you want to examine. Sentient compares up to 14 days before and after with the same weekdays; it cannot prove Sentient caused the difference.
data_description.heating_energy_price_kwh: Optional estimate used only to translate observed kWh differences into approximate daily currency changes, not actual bills or proven savings.
data_description.autooff_respect_recent_voice: Off by default. When enabled, an automatic turn-off of a light or switch is held for up to two minutes after a higher-priority guarded voice-on command. Does not apply to manual stop requests, heating, locks or alarms.

briefing.title: Briefings
briefing.description: What a briefing covers — from the BRIEFING button, by voice, or at a set time each day.

data_description.briefings: Off turns off the button, the voice tool and the service.
data_description.briefing_weather: Leave empty to use the first weather entity.
data_description.briefing_system: e.g. CPU temperature, disk use, the NAS. Pending updates are always counted.
data_description.outside_info: Sensors from other integrations read into the briefing and the evening look at tomorrow: today's electricity price, a weather warning, parcels on the way, the next school inset day. Empty, zero and 'off' readings are left out. Text from these is treated as information only.
data_description.parcel_trackers: When one says a parcel is out for delivery, it says so once and watches the door for it all day (even if parcel alerts are off); if it says delivered before anything's seen at the door, it says that too. Empty: off.
data_description.briefing_time: Optional. Only spoken if someone's home and it isn't quiet hours.
data_description.digest_time: Optional: once a day the AI sums up the timeline in a few sentences. It goes on the timeline (and to phones if chosen). Not spoken.
data_description.morning_briefing: Once a day before noon, in the room someone's in, as soon as the house sees them up and about (or, without that, the first time someone's moving after quiet hours end).
data_description.morning_briefing_areas: Optional: only give it the first time someone comes into one of these rooms in the morning, on that room's speaker — get up, wash and dress, then hear it in the kitchen or living room. Empty: wherever they are.
data_description.morning_briefing_quiet: Off: someone up and about before quiet hours end gets the briefing once they're over, the first time they're seen moving (in the morning briefing rooms, if chosen), and anything kept overnight is folded into it. On: it's given as soon as they're seen up, even in quiet hours, on just that room's speaker.
